subject: An office that closes away
hook: Is it safe to close the doors with the laptop inside?
fb:
"If I shut my laptop and printer in a cupboard, won't they overheat?" A sensible question to ask before you build an office that closes away.

The short answer: a closed laptop on charge is usually fine. Kit that runs and gets warm — a PC tower, a router, a printer in the middle of a job — needs air moving around it. So we ask what you'll keep inside at the design stage and plan in ventilation gaps or an open section where it's needed.

gbp:
Can I close my home office cupboard with my laptop and printer inside?

In most cases, a closed laptop left on charge is fine inside a cupboard. Equipment that runs and gives off heat is different: a desktop PC, a broadband router or a printer mid-job all need airflow around them.

That is why we ask exactly what you plan to keep in your office cupboard during the free design consultation. We can then plan ventilation gaps, an open section for a router, or a separate shelf for the printer, alongside cable grommets so you can close the doors without unplugging.

Every desk is made to measure and assembled in our workshop in Hanley, Stoke-on-Trent. Get in touch to talk through your setup.
